w10_T4_002652: Two neighbors, Priya and Sam, kept track of firewood, and Sam's stack always fell behind hers all week. Priya split her stack across 8 identical bundles each holding 162 logs at the start of the morning, then combined them into one pile. By midmorning, a delivery added 33 more logs. In the afternoon, a neighbor gave her 70 more logs to store for the winter. That evening, a bonfire event used up 320 logs. Late that night, 58 more logs were given away to a cold family down the street. How many logs did Priya have left?
w10_T4_002653: A juice company filled 240 liters into storage on Monday. The stock was then multiplied across 4 identical bottling lines, each producing an equal amount, bringing the total to 4 times its size. A recall then required splitting that batch evenly across 4 storage rooms, and only one room's share continued to be tracked. A separate unrelated shipment, sitting in a different warehouse, held 900 empty crates that were never filled. That tracked room's stock then grew to 4 times its size after a rush production order. The stock was next divided evenly between 2 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load was tracked further. Finally, 68 more liters were added from a backup tank before the truck left. How many liters did that truck carry?
w10_T4_002659: A toy drive collected 102 action figures by the start of the week. A local business added 53 more figures on Tuesday, and a school donated 66 more figures on Wednesday. A nearby food pantry, running its own separate campaign, gathered 300 canned goods that had nothing to do with this drive. On Thursday, a matching-donor event made the toy count grow to 7 times its size. By Friday, 153 figures had to be set aside for a different charity's request. How many action figures were left for the original toy drive?
w10_T4_002661: Two classmates, Wendy and Marco, tracked their marble collections, and Marco's total was always smaller than hers. Wendy started the semester with 122 marbles. She won 5 more marbles in a lunchtime game. She then lost 19 marbles in a bet gone wrong. Her remaining marbles were divided evenly into 4 pouches, and only one pouch was tracked afterward. That pouch then lost 15 marbles to a hole in the fabric. A trade event grew that pouch's count to 5 times its size. How many marbles were in that pouch after the trade?
w10_T4_002663: Two coworkers, Delia and Ronan, tracked their sales commissions, and Ronan's numbers stayed behind hers all week. In the morning, Delia closed 7 identical deals, each worth 108 dollars, adding up her commission for the day. By midmorning, a client dispute canceled 727 dollars worth of that commission. In the afternoon, 20 more dollars were deducted for a processing fee. That evening, a bonus program made her remaining total grow to 3 times its size. Right before closing, a second incentive made it grow to 3 times its size once more. Overnight, a correction to the books removed 70 more dollars. What was Delia's final commission?
w10_T4_002667: A charity concert began the morning with 6 ticket booths, each having sold 191 tickets by opening time, combined into one grand total. By midmorning, 56 more tickets were sold, while a nearby food stand, run separately with a dozen volunteers, wasn't included in this count. In the afternoon, a bulk group purchase made the total grow to 9 times its size. Later, 6948 tickets had to be refunded after a scheduling conflict canceled a section. That evening, 27 more tickets were sold at the door. Overnight, a final accounting correction removed 3161 tickets that had been double-counted. How many valid tickets remained after the correction?
w10_T4_002668: A recycling center started Monday with 136 pounds of aluminum cans collected. A community drive added 71 more pounds on Tuesday, while a dozen volunteers sorted plastic in a separate unrelated bin. On Wednesday, 147 pounds were shipped out to a processing plant. The remaining cans were then divided evenly across 5 collection routes, and only one route's total was tracked going forward. A weekend rush made that route's total grow to 4 times its size. Finally, 37 more pounds were added from a new drop-off bin. How many pounds of aluminum did that route have?
w10_T4_002673: Two classmates, Tara and Milo, tracked their reading minutes, and Milo's total, a dozen minutes behind at the start, never quite caught up. Tara read 118 minutes in week one. She added 49 more minutes in week two. She then added 10 more minutes in week three. A slow week four saw her total drop by 118 minutes after a family trip cut into her reading time. A strong week five added 64 more minutes. How many total minutes had Tara read by the end of week five?
w10_T4_002674: A bakery began the morning with 4 ovens, each holding 164 rolls ready to bake, combining into one big batch. By midmorning, a shipping error caused 278 rolls to be sent to the wrong store, while a dozen spare baking trays sat unused in the back room. In the afternoon, 10 more rolls came out of a late batch, and later 13 more rolls were added from a walk-in order. Since the bakery weighs dough in ounces but sells rolls by count, the head baker kept two separate logs. By evening, 28 rolls were donated to a shelter. Overnight, 253 more rolls had to be discarded after a refrigeration failure. How many rolls were left the next morning?
w10_T4_002685: A campground registered 163 campers by the start of the morning. By midmorning, 42 more campers checked in. The park then organized everyone into 8 identical group tours, each with that same total number heading out on trails, and the tour total was combined. In the afternoon, 757 campers left early due to a storm warning. Since the park tracks headcounts in whole people but the shuttle service bills per half-seat for its buses, the ranger station kept a conversion chart handy. By evening, 288 more campers checked out for the night. How many campers remained at the campground by evening?
w10_T4_002690: A parking meter held 193 minutes of prepaid time at the start of the trip. A short walk cost 2 minutes to reach the car. Feeding the meter added 74 more minutes. The remaining time was then split evenly across 5 parking zones sharing one pass, and only one zone's balance was tracked. Since meters charge in minutes but the receipt reports the total in hours, the driver always converted the number before leaving. A final minute ticked away just before the driver returned. How many minutes were left on that zone's balance?
w10_T4_002694: A car rental agency started the morning with 73 gallons of fuel in its tank. By midmorning, a delivery truck added 5 more gallons. At midday, the tank was refilled to 7 times its size for a large event. In the afternoon, the fuel was topped up again to 9 times its size for weekend reservations. Since the agency measures fuel in gallons but the invoice reports usage in liters, the manager always double-checked the conversion before billing. That evening, the fuel was split evenly across 6 identical vehicles, and only one vehicle's tank was tracked. How many gallons were in that vehicle's tank?
w10_T4_002695: Two siblings, Owen and Kira, compared their saved allowance, and Kira's stash was noticeably smaller than his. Owen started with 24 dollars saved. He earned 51 more dollars doing chores. He then earned 70 more dollars from a birthday gift. His savings were split evenly across 5 jars, and only one jar was tracked going forward. That jar then lost 13 dollars when he bought a video game. A bonus from grandma made that jar's total grow to 8 times its size. How much money was in that jar?
w10_T4_002697: Two classmates, Renee and Hugo, tracked their book-report pages, and Hugo, who had written a dozen pages less to start, never caught up. Renee had written 197 pages by the end of September. She added 35 more pages in October. A teacher's bonus assignment made her page count grow to 6 times its size. In November, 1207 pages were cut during a major revision. Finally, 55 more pages were removed after a formatting review. How many pages remained in Renee's final report?
w10_T4_002698: A print shop began the morning with 6 identical presses, each producing 96 flyers, combined into one stack. By midmorning, 32 more flyers were added from a rush order. In the afternoon, a citywide campaign made that stack grow to 7 times its size. By evening, another regional order made it grow to 9 times its size. Overnight, 13326 flyers had to be discarded after a printing defect was discovered. How many flyers were left after the discard?
w10_T4_002704: A textile mill began the day with 6 identical looms, each weaving 98 meters of fabric. The output was then doubled across 2 identical shifts working the same looms, combining their totals. A bulk order required the mill to produce 9 times that combined amount. Since the mill measures fabric in meters but the export invoice lists everything in yards, the manager always converted the totals before shipping. A final rush order required 5 times that amount to meet a deadline. How many meters of fabric did the mill need to produce for the final order?
w10_T4_002708: A food truck started the morning with 64 tacos prepped. By midmorning, 27 tacos had to be thrown out after a refrigeration issue. The remaining tacos were then multiplied across 9 identical prep trays, each holding that same amount, to meet a festival order. Since the truck measures ingredients in ounces but sells tacos by count, the owner kept two separate logs. In the afternoon, 60 more tacos were prepped fresh. By evening, 42 more tacos were added for a dinner rush. How many tacos were ready by evening?
w10_T4_002709: A construction crew started the morning with 130 bricks stacked at the site. By midmorning, a delivery truck added 69 more bricks. At midday, the crew organized the bricks into 8 identical pallets, each holding that same amount, combining them for a wall project. In the afternoon, a second shipment required 8 times that combined total for a bigger job, and since the crew measures bricks by count but the supplier invoices by weight, the foreman kept a conversion sheet handy. That evening, a final order required 7 times that afternoon total. Overnight, 7 more bricks were added from a returned pallet. How many bricks were on site the next morning?
w10_T4_002723: A trading card shop began the morning with 214 rare cards in the vault, while a dozen employees clocked in for the day, unrelated to inventory. The stock was then multiplied across 9 identical display cases, each holding that same amount, for a convention setup. A second expansion required 8 times that convention total to stock a pop-up booth. During the event, 5380 cards were sold to eager collectors. Afterward, 9977 more cards had to be returned to the warehouse after the convention ended. Finally, 79 more cards were added from a late donation. How many cards were in the vault after the donation?
w10_T4_002725: A dairy farm started the morning with 99 gallons of milk collected. The milk was then multiplied across 8 identical storage tanks, each holding that same amount, for the co-op's records. By midmorning, 60 more gallons came in from a second milking. The stock was split evenly between 2 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load was tracked, since the farm measures milk in gallons but the co-op invoice lists liters and the farmer always double-checked the conversion before selling. That truck's load then grew to 6 times its size after picking up a neighboring farm's supply. Finally, 332 gallons were sold directly to a local creamery. How many gallons were left after that sale?
w10_T4_002727: Two farmers, Delores and Nate, compared their potato harvest, and Nate's yield, a dozen sacks behind at the season's start, never caught up. Delores harvested 194 sacks of potatoes by early fall. A blight destroyed 58 sacks before they could be sold. Her remaining harvest was then multiplied across 5 identical storage sheds, each holding that same amount, for winter storage. A regional co-op order required 7 times that combined total. A final bulk contract required 5 times that new amount. Finally, 56 more sacks were added from a late harvest. How many sacks of potatoes did Delores have in total?
w10_T4_002736: Two roommates, Nina and Oscar, tracked pantry snacks, and Oscar's stash always ran lower than hers. Nina started the morning with 214 granola bars in the pantry. By midmorning, 80 bars were eaten during a study group. In the afternoon, 24 more bars were given to a neighbor. The remaining bars were split evenly between 2 shelves, and only one shelf was tracked going forward. That evening, 79 more bars were added from a grocery run. Overnight, 94 bars were packed for a camping trip. How many granola bars were left on that shelf?
w10_T4_002737: Two friends, Camille and Theo, tracked video game currency, and Theo's balance stayed lower than hers all season. Camille began with 42 gold coins in the game, and a boss battle reward made that grow to 9 times its size. A side quest then added 66 more coins. Her total was split evenly between 2 in-game accounts, and only one account was tracked. Since the game displays currency in coins but the store menu prices items in gems, Camille always checked the conversion rate before buying. A final login bonus added 68 more coins. How many coins were in that account?
w10_T4_002739: Two shopkeepers, Farah and Julian, compared their weekly earnings, and Julian's total was always smaller than hers. Farah's shop earned 140 dollars on Monday. By Tuesday, 91 dollars had to be refunded for a return. A midweek sale made her remaining total grow to 3 times its size. On Thursday, 82 dollars were spent restocking shelves. A weekend rush made that total grow to 6 times its size. Finally, 38 more dollars came in from a late sale. How much money did Farah earn by the end of the week?
w10_T4_002744: A charity book sale started the morning with 201 books on the table. By midmorning, 122 books had been sold to early shoppers. A donation drive then made the remaining stock grow to 2 times its size. A separate clothing donation bin nearby, unrelated to the book sale, collected 85 jackets that day. In the afternoon, 34 more books were added from a late drop-off. The books were split evenly between 2 tables, and only one table's stock was tracked. Finally, 31 more books were added to that table from a last-minute donor. How many books were on that table by closing?
